title: Mushroom Matar
subtitle: A home-style north Indian curry of mushrooms and peas
excerpt: Matar means peas. Paired with chestnut mushrooms in a lightly spiced tomato gravy, this is a straightforward weeknight curry that comes together in under half an hour.
sourceNotes: North Indian home-cook tradition; mushroom matar is a popular everyday vegetarian curry across Punjab and beyond.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to two months. Reheat gently from frozen with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a wide pan so the mushrooms fry rather than steam.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes good the next day. Cool and refrigerate; reheat gently before serving.

content.text: Mushroom matar is a dependable north Indian curry that works on busy evenings. The mushrooms need a hot pan and space so they brown instead of steaming in their own liquid. Frozen peas go in near the end and only need a minute or two.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer. Do not stir for 2 minutes, then toss and cook for another 2 minutes until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. Add the onion and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for one minute. Add the turmeric, ground cumin, coriander, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and the oil begins to separate.
Return the mushrooms to the pan. Stir to coat. Add 100ml of water and the salt. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Tip in the frozen peas. Stir and cook for 2 minutes until just heated through and bright green.
Stir in the garam masala. Scatter over fresh coriander and serve with rice or flatbreads.

items.symptom: The mushrooms are wet and grey rather than golden.
items.cause: The pan was overcrowded or not hot enough.
items.fix: Fry the mushrooms in a dry, very hot pan without moving them for the first 2 minutes. Cook in two batches if the pan is crowded.

items.symptom: The peas have lost their colour and gone grey.
items.cause: They were added too early and overcooked.
items.fix: Add frozen peas in the last 2 minutes only. They need just enough time to heat through.

items.cause: The tomato base was not reduced, and the mushrooms released liquid into the sauce.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for a few more minutes after adding the mushrooms. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
